questions.raw_stem: A 1 kg block subjected to two simultaneous forces (2i^ + 3j^ + 4k^) N and (3i^ - j^ - 2k^) N is moved a distance of 25 m along (3i^ - 4j^) direction. The work done in this process is _____ J.
questions.figure_locator: Page 17, Item 46, Section B (No external diagram; in-line vector formulas)
questions.solver_solution:
1. Resultant force: F_net = F_1 + F_2 = (2 + 3)i^ + (3 - 1)j^ + (4 - 2)k^ = (5i^ + 2j^ + 2k^) N.
2. Unit displacement vector along direction (3i^ - 4j^): u^ = (3i^ - 4j^) / sqrt(3^2 + (-4)^2) = (3i^ - 4j^) / 5.
3. Total displacement vector: s = 25 * u^ = 25 * (3i^ - 4j^) / 5 = (15i^ - 20j^) m.
4. Work done by net force: W = F_net . s = (5)(15) + (2)(-20) + (2)(0) = 75 - 40 = 35 J.

binding.band_reason: Direct vector addition of simultaneous constant forces combined with direction-vector normalization to construct displacement vector before scalar dot product evaluation.
binding.crux_step: Construct unit displacement vector from specified direction vector and compute scalar work as F_net . s = (5)(15) + (2)(-20) = 35 J.

tile_test.reason: The tile's shared inferential jump explicitly instructs resolving constant forces along displacement, adding signed contributions from all forces, which directly generates the crux calculation.

questions.raw_stem: A body of mass 1 kg moves along a straight line with a velocity v = 2x^2. The work done by the body during displacement from x = 0 to 5 m is _____ J.
questions.figure_locator: Page 12, Item 29, Section A (No external diagram; in-line formula v = 2x^2)
questions.solver_solution:
1. At initial position x_i = 0 m: v_i = 2(0)^2 = 0 m/s, so initial kinetic energy K_i = 0 J.
2. At final position x_f = 5 m: v_f = 2(5)^2 = 50 m/s.
3. By Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = Delta K = 1/2 m (v_f^2 - v_i^2) = 1/2 (1 kg) (50^2 - 0) = 1250 J.
(Alternative calculus route: F = m v dv/dx = 1 * (2x^2) * (4x) = 8x^3 N. W = int_0^5 8x^3 dx = [2x^4]_0^5 = 2(625) = 1250 J.)

binding.band_reason: Evaluates work done on a particle whose velocity is parameterized by position, requiring either application of the Work-Energy Theorem at position boundaries or integration of position-dependent force F(x).
binding.crux_step: Evaluate kinetic energy at the boundary positions x=0 and x=5 m to find W = Delta K = 1/2 m (50^2 - 0) = 1250 J.

tile_test.reason: Tile WEP-02 focuses strictly on geometric areas under F-x graphs and linear spring force triangles. It needs widening to cross-reference the Work-Energy Theorem (WEP-03) so students recognize that work by position-dependent forces can be obtained directly from endpoint kinetic energies without graphical quadrature.

questions.raw_stem: The rain drop of mass 1 g, starts with zero velocity from a height of 1 km. It hits the ground with a speed of 5 m/s. The work done by the unknown resistive force is _____ J. (take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.figure_locator: Page 10, Item 28, Section A (Textual stem only)
questions.solver_solution:
1. Mass of raindrop: m = 1 g = 10^-3 kg. Fall distance: h = 1 km = 1000 m.
2. Work done by gravity: W_g = m g h = (10^-3 kg)(10 m/s^2)(1000 m) = +10.0 J.
3. Change in kinetic energy: Delta K = 1/2 m v^2 - 0 = 1/2 (10^-3 kg)(5 m/s)^2 = 0.0125 J.
4. Work-Energy Theorem: W_g + W_res = Delta K ==> W_res = Delta K - W_g = 0.0125 J - 10.0 J = -9.9875 J ~= -9.98 J.

binding.band_reason: Partitions total work into conservative gravity and non-conservative air resistance, using kinetic energy difference to isolate the unknown dissipative work.
binding.crux_step: Apply Work-Energy Theorem W_g + W_res = Delta K and compute W_res = 0.0125 - 10 = -9.98 J.

tile_test.reason: WEP-03 tile not yet authored; harvesting establishes benchmark requirement for partitioning conservative and resistive work components.

questions.raw_stem: If a body of mass 1 kg falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity (v) and kinetic energy (k) on reaching the surface of earth. The values of v and k respectively are _____ . (Take radius of earth to be 6400 km and g = 9.8 m/s^2)
questions.figure_locator: Page 12, Item 31, Section A (Textual stem only)
questions.solver_solution:
1. Conservation of mechanical energy between infinity (r = infty) and Earth surface (r = R):
   E_i = K_i + U_i = 0 + 0 = 0 J.
   E_f = K_f + U_f = K_f - G M m / R = 0 ==> K_f = G M m / R.
2. Express in terms of surface gravity g = G M / R^2 ==> G M / R = g R:
   k = K_f = m g R = (1 kg)(9.8 m/s^2)(6.4 x 10^6 m) = 6.272 x 10^7 J ~= 6.27 x 10^7 J.
3. Velocity attained: 1/2 m v^2 = k ==> v = sqrt(2 g R) = sqrt(2 * 9.8 * 6.4 x 10^6) = sqrt(1.2544 x 10^8) = 11.2 x 10^3 m/s = 11.2 km/s.
4. Matching pair: 11.2 km/s; 6.27 x 10^7 J corresponds to option 691121616.

binding.band_reason: Combines non-uniform gravitational potential energy with mechanical energy conservation from an asymptotic boundary state to find speed and kinetic energy.
binding.crux_step: Set total mechanical energy E = 0 from the reference state at infinity and equate surface kinetic energy to potential energy depth K = mgR.

tile_test.reason: The tile's shared jump explicitly covers selecting the appropriate potential, fixing total energy E = K + U from a reference state, and determining maximum kinetic energy at the point of minimum accessible potential.

questions.raw_stem: A mass of 1 kg is kept on a inclined plane with 30° inclination with respect to horizontal plane and it is at rest initially. Then the whole assembly is moved up with constant velocity of 4 m/s. The work done by the frictional force in time 2 s is _____ J. (Take g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.figure_locator: Page 11, Item 28, Section A (Textual stem only)
questions.solver_solution:
1. Incline angle theta = 30° to horizontal. Since block remains at rest relative to the incline moving at constant velocity, net acceleration is zero.
2. Force balance along the incline: static friction f_s balances the component of gravity down the incline:
   f_s = m g sin(30°) = (1 kg)(10 m/s^2)(0.5) = 5 N directed upward along the incline (at 30° to horizontal).
3. Displacement of the assembly: moves vertically upward with speed v = 4 m/s for time t = 2 s:
   s = v * t = 4 * 2 = 8 m vertically upward.
4. Angle phi between friction force vector f_s and vertical displacement vector s: phi = 90° - 30° = 60°.
5. Work done by static friction in the ground frame: W_f = f_s * s * cos(60°) = 5 N * 8 m * 0.5 = 20 J.

binding.band_reason: High-transfer conceptual test proving static friction can perform positive mechanical work in an inertial frame when the supporting contact surface undergoes displacement.
binding.crux_step: Determine static friction direction and magnitude f_s = mg sin(30°) = 5 N along incline, find angle with vertical displacement phi = 60°, and evaluate W = (5)(8)cos(60°) = 20 J.

tile_test.reason: WEP-09 tile not yet authored; confirms crucial requirement that friction tile must explicitly include static friction doing non-zero work in frames where contact surfaces move.

questions.raw_stem: A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the influence of time dependent force F^ = (2t i^ + 6t^2 j^) N, where i^ and j^ are unit vectors along x and y-axis respectively. The power produced by the force at t = 2 s is _____ W.
questions.figure_locator: Page 17, Item 49, Section B (In-line force formula)
questions.solver_solution:
1. Acceleration: a(t) = F(t) / m = (2t i^ + 6t^2 j^) / 2 = t i^ + 3t^2 j^ m/s^2.
2. Initial condition 'begins to move' implies v(0) = 0.
3. Velocity at time t: v(t) = int_0^t a(t') dt' = (t^2 / 2) i^ + t^3 j^ m/s.
4. At t = 2 s:
   F(2) = 2(2) i^ + 6(2^2) j^ = 4 i^ + 24 j^ N.
   v(2) = (2^2 / 2) i^ + (2^3) j^ = 2 i^ + 8 j^ m/s.
5. Instantaneous power: P = F . v = (4)(2) + (24)(8) = 8 + 192 = 200 W.

binding.band_reason: Applies definition of instantaneous power P = F . v, requiring integration of time-varying vector acceleration to determine instantaneous velocity.
binding.crux_step: Integrate a(t) to get v(t) = (t^2/2)i^ + t^3 j^, evaluate F(2) and v(2), then compute scalar product P = (4)(2) + (24)(8) = 200 W.

tile_test.reason: WEP-08 tile not yet authored; establishes requirement for instantaneous power P = F . v with time-dependent vector forces.
